headline: Heavy Hiroshima rain; Champi weakening but Busan sailing at risk
summary: Heavy rain is forecast throughout today's Hiroshima sightseeing. Typhoon Champi has weakened, but marine conditions around the October 26 Busan call remain uncertain. No Regent-confirmed route or port changes were verified.

details: Hiroshima rain is forecast through most of Sunday, approximately 7 AM into the evening; some heavier spells around midday. Hourly probabilities mostly 80–99% during the 8:30 AM–12:30 PM tour.
Waterproof outerwear and shoes are recommended for outdoor memorial and city stops; take extra care on wet paths.

typhoon.status: Elevated marine weather concern — monitor ship announcements
typhoon.summary: Typhoon Champi has weakened to tropical-storm strength but remains a large system moving northeast through the East China Sea. Rough seas, rain and possible itinerary changes remain plausible; none are confirmed by Regent.
details: Latest JMA advisory relayed at October 25, 2026, 6:45 AM JST: Champi centered near 28.6°N, 124.3°E in the East China Sea, central pressure 996 hPa, maximum sustained wind 20 m/s (72 km/h), gusts 30 m/s (108 km/h), moving northeast at 20 km/h.
Since October 24 at 9 PM, Champi weakened from 990 hPa and 25 m/s sustained winds. Its broad wind field may still generate swell beyond the center.

JMA's October 25, 3:45 AM JST forecast projects the storm southwest of the Goto Islands around October 26 at 3 AM and as an extratropical low south of Muroto Cape by October 27 at 3 AM. Forecast track uncertainty increases after 24 hours.
Today's Hiroshima call: heavy rain and outdoor-excursion disruption; the ship's departure should be checked onboard.

October 26 Busan: elevated risk of rough seas and possible altered routing or port timing, especially during the approach from the Kanmon Strait; this is a forecast risk, not a confirmed cancellation.
October 27 Nagasaki: residual seas or knock-on schedule disruption possible; October 28 Kagoshima and October 29 Beppu: lower direct threat but possible delays if earlier calls change.
Typhoon In-fa is near the Marshall Islands and is not an immediate threat to the upcoming Japan/Korea ports.
No Regent-confirmed route change, port cancellation or excursion cancellation was verified. The publicly posted Regent itinerary remains unchanged; ship announcements take precedence.

headsUp: Hiroshima meteorologists warn of potentially severe rain and landslide risk from the evening of October 25 into October 26. Avoid flood-prone or steep areas if heavy rain develops.

Hiroshima Food Festival near Hiroshima Castle may cause crowds and limited parking. The castle notes partial parking restrictions through October 25; check local conditions and any weather-related event adjustments.
worthALook: Dated event — Hiroshima Food Festival 2026, Hiroshima Castle grounds and Hiroshima Stadium Park, Sunday October 25, 10:00 AM–5:00 PM. Free entry, local foods; only feasible after the tour if transport and ship return times allow. Rain may affect outdoor stalls.

Recurring attraction — Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum, Peace Memorial Park, 7:30 AM–7:00 PM (some early/late entry slots require advance online tickets). Indoor rainy-day option, subject to existing tour content.
Recurring attraction — Shukkeien Garden, 2-11 Kaminoboricho, Hiroshima, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. Outdoor gardens; best only if rain eases.
